beginner.title: Module 1: Basic Sentence Structure (SOV)
beginner.explanation: The most fundamental concept in Korean grammar is the sentence structure. Unlike English (Subject-Verb-Object), Korean follows a Subject-Object-Verb (SOV) order. The verb always comes at the very end. For example, 'I eat an apple' becomes 'I an apple eat' (저는 사과를 먹어요). This is the foundation for all Korean sentences.

examples.english: I drink water. (Literally: I water drink)
The cat eats fish. (Literally: Cat fish eats)

questions.question: What is the sound of the character 'ㅂ'?
What is the correct word order for 'The student reads a book'?

beginner.title: Module 2: Particles 이/가 (Subject) & 은/는 (Topic)
beginner.explanation:
Particles are essential markers in Korean. 

- 이/가 mark the SUBJECT of the sentence (who/what is doing the action). Use 이 after a consonant, and 가 after a vowel. This is often used for new information or to emphasize the subject. 

- 은/는 mark the TOPIC of the sentence ('As for...'). Use 은 after a consonant, and 는 after a vowel. This is used for introducing a topic or for stating a general fact.

examples.english: THE student is coming. (Emphasizes the student)
THE doctor is coming. (Emphasizes the doctor)
As for me, I am a student. (Topic is 'me')
Apples are delicious. (General fact about apples)

questions.question: What is the Korean word for 'Family'?
Which particle emphasizes the subject and is used after a consonant?

beginner.title: Module 3: Particles 을/를 (Object) & 에/에서 (Place)
beginner.explanation:
More essential particles! 

- 을/를 mark the OBJECT of the sentence (the thing the verb is acting on). Use 을 after a consonant, and 를 after a vowel. 

- 에 is used for a static location or destination ('at', 'to'). 
- 에서 is used for a location where an action takes place ('at', 'in').

examples.english: I read a book. ('book' is the object)
My friend watches a movie. ('movie' is the object)
I go to school. ('school' is the destination)
I work at home. ('home' is where the action happens)

questions.question: Which particle marks the object after a vowel, as in '영화___ 봐요'?
Which particle is used for a destination, as in 'I go TO school'?

beginner.title: Module 4: Present, Past, Future Tense
beginner.explanation:
Korean verbs conjugate based on tense. Here's a basic overview of the standard polite form: 

- **Present (아요/어요):** Drop '다' from the verb stem. Add 아요 if the last vowel is ㅏ or ㅗ. Add 어요 for most others. 하다 becomes 해요. 
- **Past (았어요/었어요):** Same vowel rule as present, but add 았어요 or 었어요. 하다 becomes 했어요. 
- **Future (ㄹ/을 거예요):** Add ㄹ 거예요 to stems ending in a vowel. Add 을 거예요 to stems ending in a consonant.

examples.english: To go -> Goes -> Went -> Will go
To eat -> Eats -> Ate -> Will eat
To do -> Does -> Did -> Will do

questions.question: What is the present tense of '먹다' (to eat)?
What is the future tense of '보다' (to see)?

intermediate.title: Module 5: Connectors (그리고, 그래서, 하지만)
intermediate.explanation:
Connectors link sentences together. 

- 그리고 (geurigo) means 'and' or 'and then'. It connects two related actions or statements. 
- 그래서 (geuraeseo) means 'so' or 'therefore'. It shows a cause-and-effect relationship. 
- 하지만 (hajiman) means 'but' or 'however'. It connects two contrasting ideas.

examples.korean: 저는 아침을 먹어요. 그리고 학교에 가요.
examples.english: I eat breakfast. And then I go to school.
It's raining. So I'm at home.
Korean is difficult. But it's fun.

questions.question: Which connector shows contrast, like in 'It's expensive, ___ it's good.'?
Fill in the blank: 'I studied hard. ___ I passed the test.'

intermediate.title: Module 6: Honorifics (-(으)시) & Suggestions (-(으)ㄹ까요?)
intermediate.explanation:
Politeness is key in Korean. 

- -(으)시- is a particle added to verb stems to show respect to the person you're talking about. Use -시- after a vowel, and -으시- after a consonant. 

- -(으)ㄹ까요? is used to make a suggestion or ask for an opinion ('Shall we...?'). Use -ㄹ까요 after a vowel, and -을까요 after a consonant.

examples.english: The teacher reads a book. (Respectful)
The boss is not here now. (Respectful)
Shall we watch a movie together?
What shall we eat for dinner?

questions.question: How do you say 'Shall we go to the market?'
Which is the correct honorific form for 'The doctor sees' (의사가 보다)?

intermediate.title: Module 7: Expressing Desire (-고 싶다)
intermediate.explanation: To express what you want to do, you attach -고 싶다 (go sipda) to a verb stem. This is equivalent to 'I want to...' in English. It's a very common and useful pattern for expressing your desires.

examples.english: I want to watch a movie.
I want to go to Korea.
I want to eat Kimchi.

questions.question: How do you say 'I want to study'?
What does '책을 읽고 싶어요' mean?
options: I want to read a book
questions.answer: I want to read a book

intermediate.title: Listening Practice: At the Cafe
intermediate.transcript:
A: 안녕하세요. 뭐 드시겠어요? (Hello. What would you like to have?) 
B: 아이스 아메리카노 한 잔 주세요. (One iced americano, please.)

questions.question: Where is this conversation taking place?
What did person B order?

intermediate.title: Listening Practice: Asking for Directions
intermediate.transcript:
A: 실례합니다. 지하철역이 어디에 있어요? (Excuse me. Where is the subway station?) 
B: 이 길로 쭉 가세요. 그러면 오른쪽에 있어요. (Go straight down this road. Then it's on your right.) 
A: 감사합니다! (Thank you!)

questions.question: What is person A looking for?
Where is the subway station located?

advanced.title: Module 8: Complex Connectors (-(으)면, -아/어도, -ㄹ/을 때)
advanced.explanation:
These connectors allow for more complex sentences. 

- -(으)면 (myeon) means 'if' or 'when'. Use -면 after a vowel, and -으면 after a consonant. 
- -아/어도 (ado/eodo) means 'even if' or 'even though'. 
- -ㄹ/을 때 (l/eul ttae) means 'when' or 'at the time of'.

examples.english: If I have time, I will watch a movie.
Even though I'm busy, I always eat breakfast.
When I was a student, I studied hard.

questions.question: How do you say 'If it rains...'?
What does '학생일 때' mean?

advanced.title: Module 9: Quoting Sentences (-ㄴ/는)다고 하다
advanced.explanation: To report or quote what someone else said, you use the 'indirect quotation' grammar pattern. For descriptive verbs (adjectives), it's -다고 하다. For action verbs, it's -ㄴ/는다고 하다.

examples.english: She said that the weather is cold.
My friend says they are watching a movie.

advanced.title: Module 10: Reading Practice
advanced.content: 한국 사회는 최근 몇 년간 빠르게 변화하고 있습니다. 특히, 기술 발전과 함께 사람들의 생활 방식도 많이 달라졌습니다. 예를 들어, 스마트폰이 없으면 하루를 보내기 어려울 정도입니다. 이러한 변화는 긍정적인 면도 있지만, 부정적인 문제들도 있습니다. 여러분의 생각은 어떻습니까?

questions.question: What is the main topic of this passage?
According to the passage, what is difficult to live without?
